title: Research Tool Integration: Building and Using Data Extraction Tools
purpose: Standardize how research tools are built, tested, indexed, and used by agent teams. Ensures tools are discoverable, token-efficient, and integrated into research pipelines.

tool_discovery.title: Step 1: Find Existing Tools Before Building New Ones
tool_discovery.overview: Before writing any data extraction code, check what tools already exist.

steps.action: Check the scripts index for existing tools
steps.command: python3 -c "import json; idx=json.load(open('storage/scripts/index.json')); [print(f'{s["id"]}: {s["name"]} — {s["description"][:80]}') for s in idx['scripts'] if s['category']=='data-collection']"
steps.rationale: Avoid rebuilding tools that already exist.

steps.action: Check knowledge base for prior research on the data source
steps.rationale: Previous teams may have documented API access patterns, rate limits, or workarounds.

steps.action: Check the sources catalog for API definitions
steps.rationale: Data source definitions with endpoints and schemas may already exist.

tool_development_checklist.title: Step 2: Tool Development Standards
tool_development_checklist.overview: All research tools must meet these standards before being committed.

requirements.requirement: Dual interface: CLI for manual use + Python API for agent import
requirements.example: python3 tool.py <command> [args]  AND  from tool import ToolClass; t = ToolClass()

requirements.details: All network queries must be cached locally. Filenames must handle special chars (/ : ? etc). Cache must be clearable.
If the API supports batch queries, the tool must implement them. Single-item queries should be a convenience wrapper around batch.
requirements.rationale: Batch queries are typically 10-100x more efficient than individual queries.

requirements.details: Provide at minimum: full JSON (for programmatic use), compact JSON (short keys, no whitespace), and LLM format (newline-separated, compressed URLs).

format_guide.compact_json: Short keys (e: external, i: internal, c: categories), separators=(',',':')
format_guide.url_compression: Use prefix shorthand (wa: for web.archive.org, ax: for arxiv.org, doi: for doi.org, etc.)

requirements.details: Track API calls, cache hits, total items processed. Report via stats command or get_stats() method.
Handle HTTP redirects, API errors, empty responses, and malformed data gracefully. Never crash on bad input — return empty results.
Include sleep delays between batch queries. Document known rate limits in the tool's docstring and KB entry.

tool_registration.title: Step 3: Registering a New Tool
tool_registration.overview: Every tool must be indexed in three places for discoverability.

steps.action: Update knowledge-base/index.json with the new KB entry
Add usage instructions to the SOP catalog if the tool is complex
steps.when: If the tool has >3 commands or requires specific workflow knowledge

using_tools_in_research.title: Step 4: Using Tools in Research Routines
using_tools_in_research.overview: Standard workflow for research teams using data extraction tools.

actions: Identify the data source and check for existing tools (Step 1)
If tool exists: use it. If not: build one following Step 2 standards
Run batch extraction first (covers the most ground fastest)
Use cached data for subsequent operations
Export in LLM format when feeding data to agents (saves ~30% tokens)
Export in full JSON when data needs programmatic processing
Use compact/LLM exports to stay within agent context limits
Document gaps in coverage for future runs
Commit cache files (enables instant re-use by future teams)
Create/update KB entry with methodology and findings

token_efficiency_mandate.title: Token Efficiency Requirements for All Research Tools
token_efficiency_mandate.overview: Agents MUST use token-efficient formats when passing data between agents or injecting data into prompts.
rules: ALWAYS use LLM export format when feeding data into agent prompts
ALWAYS use compact JSON when storing intermediate results
NEVER use full/pretty JSON in agent-to-agent communication
URL compression is MANDATORY for any tool that handles URLs
Internal link lists should use pipe-separated format (title1|title2) not JSON arrays
Metadata should use single-letter keys in compact exports (d: description, c: categories, e: external, i: internal)

egress_testing_protocol.title: Pre-Development Egress Testing
egress_testing_protocol.overview: Before building a tool for any external API, test accessibility first.

steps.note: Some URLs work via WebFetch but not curl, and vice versa

steps.action: Document results in a test matrix before committing to development
If blocked: check for alternative endpoints, mirrors, or SPARQL interfaces

known_workarounds.wikidata: Blocked by egress — use DBpedia owl:sameAs cross-refs instead
known_workarounds.nature.com: Blocked — use doi.org or Semantic Scholar for paper metadata
